title: Expose governed successor and quarantine transition command
outOfScope: Changing a predecessor Contract, Summary, Outcome, archive, or branch; the command may create only its declared successor receipt after validation.
Implementing successor product work, provider mutation, archive, merge, release, or branch deletion.
Changing unrelated Work Item scheduling or verification policy.

sources.reason: Defines the missing public successor/quarantine lifecycle command and required rejection cases.
Concrete immutable blocked-predecessor Outcome shape; #704 remains active and is read-only external evidence.
Contains the existing transition primitive that needs a validated public entrypoint and projections.

declaredIntent.summary: Expose the existing blocked-predecessor transition as a governed, evidence-bound lifecycle command.

riskAssessment.reason: A permissive transition could authorize successor work or alter another active Work Item without a blocked Outcome, exact Issue binding, authority, or installed-template parity.
riskAssessment.unknownsReviewReason: The issue, predecessor evidence format, public command inputs, failure boundary, and verification are all available locally; no product decision is missing.

reasons: Cross-Work-Item lifecycle evidence and authorization boundary require full verification.

override.approvalEvidence: User authorized automatic execution and supersession/quarantine in this thread.
override.reason: Strict lifecycle command review without provider operations.
notRunChecks: Release checks are inapplicable: no release-owned resource is touched.

executionDecision.reason: The user authorized automatic execution and explicitly authorized supersession/quarantine, recorded below and in the raw request.

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: User granted automatic execution and supersession/quarantine authority; it is limited to a validated receipt created by this command and never authorizes predecessor rewrites, archive, merge, release, or branch deletion.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record the authorization and public-boundary implementation checkpoints.

acceptance: `make ai-transition-to-successor` and the distributed Makefile invoke a public CLI that requires an explicit predecessor Outcome, predecessor and distinct successor identities, an Issue URL in this repository, a non-empty recorded authority, a reason, and exactly `superseded` or `quarantined`; every invalid input fails closed before a receipt write.

A successful CLI invocation writes exactly one receipt at the declared active predecessor receipt path, binding the exact blocked Outcome digest, predecessor/successor identities, linked Issue, authority, reason, and mode; it never changes predecessor Contract/Summary/Outcome, archive, Git state, provider state, or release state.

Status and doctor project a validated successor receipt as a yellow transition route, retain the predecessor blocked/red state, and expose a recovery condition without claiming archive, merge, or completion.

Focused red-first tests prove acceptance, missing authority, foreign Issue, non-blocked predecessor, same identity, malformed/foreign receipt, and installed-template command parity; source and installed runtime reject missing components fail closed.

Canonical English/Japanese Cockpit and lifecycle reference documentation state command syntax, authority and receipt ownership boundary, traffic-light meaning, and the explicit non-authorization limitations.
guidelines: A public lifecycle command must validate every cross-Work-Item identity and authorization before writing evidence.
Keep lifecycle truth fail-closed: a successor route is not archive, merge, release, or completion authorization.
Maintain source and installed-template parity, including documented command surfaces and tests.
Do not import internal modules from other features.

intent.problem: The lifecycle runtime has `transition_to_successor()` but no public governed command or declared receipt ownership route. A blocked Work Item therefore cannot consume authorized supersession/quarantine without an out-of-scope direct library write.
constraints: Require a blocked Outcome digest, exact successor identity, in-repository Issue, and recorded user authority.
Make the only mutation a receipt at an explicitly declared/validated path.
Do not implement a manual workaround, provider mutation, archive rewrite, merge, release, or branch operation.
intent.rationale: An executable, evidence-bound transition resolves the lifecycle deadlock while retaining the predecessor’s immutable red Outcome and making the successor route auditable.

rawUserRequest: Execute the plan to completion. I authorize automatic execution, captured in every Work Item Contract. If a process problem occurs, create a corrective Work Item first; do not use temporary repairs. I authorize supersession/quarantine and require Outcome red/yellow/green visibility.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A blocked predecessor has a distinct corrective successor, repository Issue, recorded authority, and valid transition mode.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The CLI writes only a digest-bound receipt and doctor/status surface a yellow route while the Outcome remains red/blocked.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Use a temporary repository fixture to execute the public CLI and inspect only the declared receipt mutation and projections.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Authority, Issue repository, predecessor state/digest, successor identity, mode, or receipt ownership is invalid.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The CLI returns non-zero and creates or changes no receipt or predecessor evidence.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Create focused red-first parameterized CLI and projection regressions.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: An installed adopter has the lifecycle runtime but missing or mismatched command target/catalog entry.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Parity validation or command invocation fails closed rather than claiming the source capability is installed.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Extend isolated-adopter parity tests for the Make target, runtime catalog, and public CLI.

rollbackNote: Revert this Work Item diff; no command invocation against repository evidence is part of this implementation, and all tests use temporary fixtures.
